projects.name: Ma'ale Gilboa Agrivoltaic Project
projects.summary: A commercial-scale agrivoltaic site combining solar generation with table grapes, lychee, mango and field crops at Kibbutz Ma'ale Gilboa.

organizations.name: Kibbutz Ma'ale Gilboa / Ma'ale Gilboa Energy

officialPlanLinks.rationale: The official record and project evidence identify the same locality and initiative. The official boundary is about 148.8 dunam versus about 150 dunam in the developer permit release; the Israel Land Authority decision identifies Kibbutz Ma'ale Gilboa, parcel 20903/38 and 148.420 dunam. Planning status was not used to infer physical stage.

dataGaps: Published capacity values use unresolved nameplate, expected, plan and grid-connection bases.
A single canonical AC/DC capacity value is therefore not published.
Storage presence for this exact installation is not publicly evidenced in the reviewed sources.

claims.explanation: A Doral public-company presentation identifies commercial operation. A later independent report describes the panels generating electricity while crops are being harvested beneath them; a technical article describes the first year of operation.

roles.organization: Kibbutz Ma'ale Gilboa / Ma'ale Gilboa Energy

claims.explanation: The developer release, technical article and independent reporting consistently identify Doral and the Ma'ale Gilboa agricultural organization in the initiative.
Multiple sources identify the crop program. Crop presence is time-bounded and is not treated as a permanent site attribute.

The reviewed sources report 9 MWp in a 2025 operational portfolio slide, a 10 MW grid-connection basis in the 2022 land decision, and both 10 MWp expected and roughly 12 MW narrative values on developer pages. Their AC/DC, connection and nameplate bases are not reconciled, so no single canonical capacity is published.

Land allocation recommended for the dual-use solar facility
Developer reports signed construction permit
Commercial operation reported in public-company presentation
Independent report observes active electricity generation and crops
Claim set independently reviewed and published

projects.name: Beit HaEmek Agrivoltaic Project
projects.summary: A reviewed agrivoltaic initiative at Kibbutz Beit HaEmek combining solar infrastructure with avocado cultivation. The latest physical-stage evidence supports construction but is now stale and requires recheck.

officialPlanLinks.rationale: The Israel Land Authority notice explicitly names Beit HaEmek and plan 201-0961607, matching the AGRO record and the project identity used in Doral's portfolio disclosure and the later published interview. Planning status was not used to infer physical stage.

dataGaps: The latest reviewed physical-stage observation is older than the 90-day construction freshness window.
The reviewed sources do not confirm commissioning or grid connection for the full agrivoltaic project.
The 8 MWp and 40 MWh figures are developer-reported and have not been independently reconciled with as-built records.

claims.explanation: The developer portfolio disclosure places the Beit HaEmek initiative in physical delivery, while a later published interview describes installed agrivoltaic panels but says execution and grid connection of the large project were delayed. Construction is the safest supported stage; operation of the full project is not claimed. The latest observation has passed the 90-day construction freshness window.
The public-company disclosure and published interview consistently identify the Doral–Kibbutz Beit HaEmek partnership; the land-rights notice independently fixes the initiative to the exact plan.

The developer portfolio identifies avocado and the later interview describes the site's agricultural–solar implementation. Crop presence remains a time-bounded observation, not a permanent outcome claim.

Doral reports 8 MWp solar capacity and 40 MWh storage for Beit HaEmek. These are retained with their units and developer-source qualifier; they are not treated as independently verified as-built values.

timeline.label: Plan received by the planning system
Plan published for approval
Developer portfolio reports physical delivery with 8 MWp and 40 MWh
Israel Land Authority publishes exact-plan land-rights notice
Published interview describes installed panels and delayed execution/grid connection
Construction-stage Claim passes its 90-day freshness window

projects.name: Eilot Agrivoltaic Project
projects.summary: A reviewed Shikun & Binui Energy–Kibbutz Eilot initiative for field-crop land, with 12 MW solar and 84 MWh storage reported by the developer. Current evidence supports permits and procurement, not construction.

officialPlanLinks.rationale: The exact plan number appears in the official AGRO record, the Shikun & Binui Energy planning annex and the Israel Land Authority notice for Kibbutz Eilot. The developer disclosure identifies the Eilot initiative and its reported system scale. The official geometry is about 259.7 dunam, the plan record's total proposed area is about 240.568 dunam, and the land transaction is 251,057 square metres; these are preserved as different area concepts. Planning status was not used to infer physical stage.

dataGaps: No reviewed public source establishes that physical construction has started; the developer's ground-works timing is forward-looking.
The 12 MW solar and 84 MWh storage figures are developer-reported planned values, not independently verified as-built capacity.
The official geometry, proposed plan area and land-transaction area use different boundaries or legal concepts and are not collapsed into one footprint.

claims.explanation: The developer reports Ministry of Agriculture approval and expected ground works during 2026. A later Israel Land Authority notice records an exact-plan land-rights transaction for Kibbutz Eilot. Together these support a current permits/procurement stage. Neither source proves that physical construction has started, so construction is not claimed.

The exact-plan technical annex names Shikun & Binui Energy as the commissioning party, while the land-rights notice fixes the transaction to Kibbutz Eilot. The role labels remain editorial interpretations of those public records.

The developer says the Ministry of Agriculture approval concerns establishment on field-crop land. This documents the approved agricultural setting; it is not treated as an observation of crops currently growing beneath an operating system.

Shikun & Binui Energy reports 12 MW solar capacity and 84 MWh storage for Eilot. The values retain their original units and developer-source qualifier and are not presented as independently verified as-built capacity.

timeline.label: Plan received by the planning system
Plan approval published
Developer reports agriculture approval, 12 MW solar and 84 MWh storage, with ground works expected during 2026
Israel Land Authority publishes exact-plan land-rights notice
Project published at permits/procurement stage; construction not evidenced

projects.name: Kfar Pines Agrivoltaic Project
projects.summary: A reviewed EDF Renewables–Moshav Kfar Pines initiative. The last supported progress is the December 2024 plan approval; no reviewed evidence establishes physical delivery, so the planning-stage claim is stale.

officialPlanLinks.rationale: The official AGRO record and approval notice identify plan 351-0789537 and the approximately 97.4-dunam Kfar Pines site. The exact-plan environmental annex identifies EDF Renewables, while the two published reports independently identify the same EDF–Moshav Kfar Pines initiative and approximately 100-dunam site. Planning status was not used to infer physical construction or operation.

dataGaps: No reviewed project-specific public evidence after the December 2024 plan approval establishes a building permit, procurement, construction, commissioning or operation.
Published planning-phase capacity figures conflict: 12–16 MW in 2021 versus 6.4 MW with a storage option in 2022; their design bases are not reconciled.
Vineyards and citrus were reported as design preferences in 2021, not as current crops beneath an installed agrivoltaic system.
The official geometry is about 97.4 dunam; published reports also describe about 97–100 dunam total and 77 dunam for the solar system. These area concepts are not collapsed.

claims.explanation: The last reviewed evidence of project progress is planning activity culminating in approval of the exact plan in December 2024. Older independent reporting corroborates the EDF–Moshav initiative and its planning process. No reviewed source proves a later permit or any physical works, and the 180-day freshness window has expired; planning is therefore a stale last-evidenced stage, not a claim that the site remains unchanged.

The exact-plan annex and two independent reports consistently identify EDF Renewables as developer and Moshav Kfar Pines as the agricultural land partner during planning. This is a historical role claim, not evidence of current ownership or operation.

A 2021 planning-phase report described vineyards as the preferred crop and citrus as an alternative. This stale design intention is retained as a claimed value and is not evidence that either crop is currently present beneath panels.

The 2021 report gives a planned range of 12–16 MW, while the 2022 report gives 6.4 MW with a storage option. Neither is an as-built value and their design bases are not reconciled, so no canonical installed capacity is published.

reportedValues.qualifier: planning-phase value reported in 2022; storage option mentioned

timeline.label: Plan received by the planning system

Plan deposit published in the official register
Published report describes opposition and a conflicting 6.4 MW design value
Plan approval published

Project published with stale-stage and capacity-conflict warnings

projects.summary: A reviewed Energix–Moshav Gan Hashomron initiative with an 8 MW planning-phase design. A dedicated project company was registered in August 2025, but no reviewed evidence establishes a permit or physical works, so planning remains the stale last-evidenced stage.

The exact-plan local committee protocol identifies the Solair Energix partnership and the Gan Hashomron agricultural submitter. TheMarker independently describes the same Energix–Moshav initiative at approximately 90 dunam, and a dedicated Energix Gan Hashomron project company was registered in 2025. Planning status and corporate formation were not used to infer physical construction.

dataGaps: No reviewed public source establishes a building permit, procurement milestone, construction start, commissioning or operation.
The dedicated project-company registration is evidence of continued project organization, not physical delivery.
The 8 MW figure is a planning-phase reported design and has not been reconciled with a permit, grid-connection record or as-built value.
No publishable source identifies the crop group intended or currently cultivated beneath an installed system.

claims.explanation: The approved exact plan and planning protocol establish the initiative, while the August 2025 registration of a dedicated Energix Gan Hashomron project company shows continued project organization. None of the reviewed sources proves a permit or physical works. Planning is therefore the safest last-evidenced stage, and its 180-day freshness window has expired.

The exact-plan protocol and independent reporting consistently identify the Energix development role and Gan Hashomron agricultural partnership. These are historical planning-phase roles, not a claim about the current operator.
TheMarker reports an 8 MW design for the Gan Hashomron initiative. This is retained as a planning-phase reported value and is not presented as permitted, connected or as-built capacity.

officialPlanLinks.rationale: This link is a reviewed inference from a uniquely matching evidence set: the official record describes the Beer Milka 250.252-dunam combined ground-mounted photovoltaic and agrivoltaic plan, while Meshek Energy's project lead discloses approval for deposit of a combined facility at Beer Milka and the planning consultant independently identifies the same 250-dunam Beer Milka design and Meshek Energy partnership. No competing reviewed Beer Milka plan matches that locality, footprint, combined technology and milestone. Planning approval was not used to infer a permit, construction or operation.

dataGaps: No reviewed public source establishes a building permit, procurement milestone, construction start, commissioning or operation.
The September 2025 statutory approval is an OfficialPlan status and does not refresh or replace the separate actual implementation-stage Claim.
No publishable source provides permitted, connected or as-built capacity.
The reviewed sources describe agricultural and circular-economy intent but do not establish the crop group that would be cultivated beneath an installed system.

The later official approval remains on the regulatory track: it does not prove a permit or physical works and therefore does not refresh the actual-stage evidence. Planning is the safest last-evidenced stage, and its 180-day freshness window has expired.

The developer-side disclosure identifies Meshek Energy and the Beer Milka agricultural community, while the planning consultant independently identifies the Meshek Energy partnership and the same unique 250-dunam combined design. These are historical planning-phase roles, not a claim about a current operator.

aliases: The Moshav Yesha Field Crop Project
projects.summary: An Enlight Agro-Solar research project in an active field at Moshav Yesha, launched in 2024 and documented through multiple field-crop cycles and a wine-vineyard planting. The AgriPV array is kept separate from the co-located conventional solar and storage facilities in the site's wider master plan.

site.centroidBasis: Approximate Moshav Yesha reference point; the exact field footprint is not publicly resolved.

dataGaps: No reviewed public source provides an exact project polygon, parcel identifiers or a statutory plan number; the map therefore uses an explicitly approximate locality point.
The public project page does not state a standalone solar capacity for the Agro-Solar array. Co-located storage and conventional ground-mounted PV are not attributed to this AgriPV project.
Developer yield statements are not published as verified outcomes because numerical methods, complete results and an independently reviewable dataset were not located.

claims.explanation: Enlight's current Agro-Solar page identifies a distinct active-field project at Moshav Yesha, states that it launched in 2024 and documents agricultural cycles through June 2026. The exact date of the page's latest physical observation is not stated, so the stage is time-bounded rather than given an invented observation date.
The project is published by Enlight as its Moshav Yesha Agro-Solar initiative. Moshav Yesha is retained as the agricultural site partner; the public page does not name an individual farm operator.

The developer documents several completed or underway crop cycles and a wine vineyard planted beneath the array. The crop list is evidence of agricultural use, not a verified yield or agronomic-impact result.

claims.value: Agro-Solar field array only; co-located conventional PV and storage remain separate assets
claims.explanation: Enlight states that the site also includes large-scale storage and a ground-mounted solar facility under an integrated master plan. Those assets are not silently merged into the AgriPV project or used to infer its capacity.

The two panel-coverage percentages are described as different but are not quantified in the reviewed public source.

Because no newer physical observation was located, the January evidence is published as a stale last-evidenced research-pilot stage.
The launch account names the research operator and core project partners. Funding and support bodies are retained in source provenance rather than converted into ownership or operating roles.

claims.value: Two research systems with different, publicly unquantified solar-panel coverage ratios
